cohort: 100 pregnant women, 50 with obesity (BMI >30 kg/m2) and 50 with normal BMI, recruited from a tertiary care hospital in Kurnool, India
finding: Maternal obesity was associated with increased rates of hypertensive disease, GDM, cesarean sections, wound infections, DVT, preterm deliveries, anemia, and hypothyroidism in mothers, and higher rates of NICU admissions and preterm births in newborns.
mod_finding: Among cesarean deliveries, a significantly higher proportion of obese women (20%) required prolonged hospital stay (>7 days) compared to women with normal BMI (2%).
